newsitem.title: UK: Chubb Security says in talks, may get offer.
newsitem.headline: Chubb Security says in talks, may get offer.

text.p: Britain's Chubb Security Plc said on Thursday it was in talks that may lead to a recommended offer for the company.
The security services firm said it did not expect such an offer to exceed a value of 450 pence per share.
Chubb's shares shot up more than 20 percent, gaining 70.5 pence to 411.5 to rank as the London Stock Exchange's top percentage gainer by 1115 GMT.

Chubb's statement came after a comment in the Financial Times highlighted its strong brands as a potential attraction to a buyer, possibly from the United States. Chubb said it expected to make a further announcement soon.

The company, which provides electronic and physical security services, previously said two acquisitions would dilute full-year earnings by 3.0 million pounds ($4.90 million). In December, Chubb said analysts' forecasts for its pretax profits for the year ended March 31 were 103 to 104 million pounds, excluding the dilutive effect of acquisitions.
Chubb's previously-announced first-half results, which showed a a nearly four percent rise in pretax profits to 46.1 million pounds, came in at the low end of market expectations.
Last year, Chubb bought James Hardie Building Services from Australia's James Hardie Industries Ltd and acquired MSS Security from Mayne Nickless Ltd. ($1=.6120 Pound)
